question: How is the CGTMSE annual guarantee fee charged for facilities sanctioned on or after 1 April 2025?
answer: The CGTMSE annual guarantee fee is charged on the guaranteed amount for the first year [R-CG-C-396#section#14]. For the remaining tenure of the credit facilities, it is charged on the outstanding amount [R-CG-C-396#section#14].

question: What is the maximum credit facility per borrower covered by a CGTMSE guarantee?
answer: The maximum credit facility per borrower covered by a CGTMSE guarantee is ₹500 lakh for secured credit facilities and ₹200 lakh for unsecured credit facilities [R-CG-C-396#section#8].

question: Can a medium enterprise get a CGTMSE credit guarantee?
answer: Yes, a medium enterprise can get a CGTMSE credit guarantee as the CGTMSE is set up to facilitate the flow of credit to the MSE sector [R-CG-C-397#section#1].

question: At what GST rate is a loan processing fee charged?
answer: The loan processing fee is liable to GST as supply of services [R-GST-C-109#section#752]. The fee is generally a one-time charge that lenders levy on applicants when they apply for a loan [R-GST-C-109#section#752].

question: Is GST charged on the interest on a loan?
answer: GST is not charged on the interest on a loan [R-GST-C-109#section#744].

question: Within how many days must a buyer pay a micro or small enterprise supplier at the latest?
answer: The buyer must pay the supplier within 45 days from the date of acceptance or the day of deemed acceptance [R-RBI-04#section#26][R-RBI-05#section#4].

question: What interest is due when a buyer pays a micro or small enterprise supplier late?
answer: The buyer shall be liable to pay compound interest with monthly rests to the supplier on the amount from the appointed day or, on the date agreed on, at three times of the Bank Rate notified by Reserve Bank [R-MSME-01#section#70].

question: How does income tax treat an expense owed to a micro or small enterprise supplier that is paid late?
answer: The interest paid on late payment to a micro or small enterprise supplier is not allowed as a deduction from income under the Income-tax Act, 1961 [R-MSME-01#section#75].

question: What is TReDS and what does it do for MSMEs?
answer: TReDS is an electronic platform for facilitating the financing/discounting of trade receivables of MSMEs through multiple financiers [R-RBI-FAQ-003#section#1]. It helps MSMEs by enabling them to convert their trade receivables into finance [R-SANSAD-019#section#5].

question: What is the RBI policy repo rate as of November 2026?
answer: The RBI policy repo rate as of November 2026 is 5.50 per cent [R-RATE-02-REPO#section#0].

question: Who approves a working-capital proposal above ₹1.5 crore under our approval matrix?
answer: The VP, Finance approves a working-capital proposal above ₹1.5 crore [FAQ-008#section#0][POL-APPROVAL-MATRIX-v1#section#0].

question: How does our current working-capital policy size the recommended facility?
answer: The recommended facility is calculated as peak cumulative shortfall plus minimum cash buffer minus undrawn sanctioned limits minus confirmed mitigations, never below zero, rounded up to the next ₹1,00,000 [POL-WC-POL-v3#section#0].

question: Which KYC directions apply to our commercial-bank lender?
answer: The KYC directions applicable to our commercial-bank lender are the Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Know Your Customer) Directions, 2025 [R-RBI-09#section#12].

question: Do the NBFC Responsible Business Conduct Directions govern the KFS on our commercial-bank loan?
answer: The Key Fact Statement (KFS) on our commercial-bank loan is governed by the Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025 [R-RBI-HIST-021#section#30].
